## Correction from the filer: the Impact section above is too broad

I wrote "any PR whose base includes the breakage cannot go green on `Build Docs`". That is wrong, and the title said the same thing — I have narrowed the title to drop "blocking every PR based after it". The defect and the `main` evidence are unchanged; only the blast radius is.

### The measurement that corrects it

PR #5669 is based on `9986f9114` — the **same base as #5665**, so it includes the breakage. Its `Build Docs` job `97004132812` reports **`success`**, 08:13:01→08:13:12: **11 seconds**. The log ends:

```
No docs-related files changed. Skipping the steps below; this check still reports.
```

The job is path-filtered *inside itself*, at the step level, not at the job or workflow level (`ci.yml`, step `Check for docs changes`). On a `pull_request` event it runs `git diff --name-only base.sha...head.sha -- 'apps/site/' 'content/'`, and every subsequent step carries `if: steps.docs-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'`.

- #5665 edits `content/docs/components/basic/{div,span}.mdx` → `should_run=true` → real site build → **failure**, 3m26s.
- #5669 touches only `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` → `should_run=false` → **success**, 11s, nothing built.

### Corrected impact

**A PR whose base includes the breakage fails `Build Docs` only if its diff touches `apps/site/**` or `content/**`.** Every other PR reports green on that check without building the site.

This also revises the "Why it went unnoticed" section above. I attributed #5656/#5659/#5662's green `Build Docs` to their bases predating the breakage. Their bases *were* older, but that was not the only reason and possibly not the operative one — #5669 shows the path filter alone is sufficient to report green on a poisoned base. Four PRs merging between 01:56Z and 07:31Z while `main`'s own push runs were already red is not a race; it is the filter.

`main`'s push runs are unfiltered in this respect (the same step returns `should_run=true` early on any non-`pull_request` event), which is why the failure is visible there and nowhere else.

### A second reading, recorded as measurement + inference

That early return is worth stating in full, because it bears on whether the merge queue would have caught this:

```
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != 'pull_request' ]; then
  echo 'should_run=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo 'Not a pull request: push is filtered at the trigger, and a merge_group build is the last validation before main. Building the site.'
```

So a **queue** build builds the site on every PR regardless of paths, and `main`'s `ci.yml` does subscribe the queue — `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`, lines 50–51, verified against `origin/main` rather than a local checkout.

**Measured:** `GET /actions/runs?event=merge_group` returns `total_count: 0` — for `ci.yml`, and again with no workflow filter, i.e. repo-wide. **Control:** the identical call with `event=push` on `ci.yml` returns `total_count: 3944`, so the event filter is functional and the zero is a real reading.

**Inference, flagged as such:** if no `merge_group` run has ever existed, that unconditional branch has never been exercised and the queue is validating neither this check nor any other — which is the precise hole `ci.yml`'s own comment block says #3523 closed. I have **not** established why the subscription is present in the file yet produces no runs, and I am not guessing. The distinguishing measurement is the repository ruleset's merge-queue configuration — whether a queue is actually engaged for `main` and what its required-check set is — which I cannot read with this session's access. I am deliberately not filing a card on an inference; if someone with that access confirms it, it deserves its own, and it is a larger problem than this one.

## Follow-up: the "inference" in my last comment is an already-open finding — **#4986**

In the correction above I recorded the zero-`merge_group`-runs reading as measurement, flagged the conclusion drawn from it as inference, and said I would not file a card on an inference. That was the right call on the evidence I had, but the reason it was not worth filing turns out to be stronger: **#4986 already covers it, is open, and has more than I did** — including that the queue's required set was measured directly and does not contain the four test shards, `Type Check`, or `Lint`.

I found it on the dedupe search, before filing. Cross-referencing rather than restating.

Two things I have added to #4986 rather than here:

1. **The condition is still true today** — `event=merge_group` returns `total_count: 0` repo-wide against a control of 3944 for `event=push`, and `main`'s `ci.yml` does carry the `merge_group` subscription (lines 50–51).
2. **A second, independent line of evidence: the enqueue→merge timings.** #5669/#5670/#5671/#5672 each went from `pull_request.enqueued` to `merged_at` in **15–17 seconds**, while the pull-request lane's run of that same workflow on those same commits took 5m49s–8m25s for `Type Check` alone and ~10 minutes for the test shards. A queue build that ran `ci.yml` cannot finish in fifteen seconds.

### Why this matters *for this card*

It supplies the missing half of the "why did four merges carry this forward" question.

The PR-lane `Build Docs` is path-filtered inside the job, so a PR touching no docs path reports green in 11 s having built nothing. The **queue** copy is not path-filtered — the same step returns `should_run=true` early on any non-`pull_request` event, under the comment *"a merge_group build is the last validation before main"*. **A working queue build would have run a real site build on every one of those four PRs and caught this at the first merge.**

So this breakage is a concrete cash-in of #4986, in the same shape as the 2026-08-07 incident `ci.yml`'s own comments record — just quieter, because it landed on a job most PRs never really run.

The defect in this card is unchanged and still needs its own fix: the bisect window (after `aa3b81062`, at or before `7e811687a`) and the two candidate causes stand.

## The bisect window collapses to one commit, and it is not ambiguous

The card's window is *after `aa3b81062`, at or before `7e811687a`* — **six commits**. Exactly one of them touches `pnpm-lock.yaml` or any `package.json`:

```
7e811687a  refactor(app-shell): paramToField's reference-bearing rule … (#5655)
71ee4959e  fix(app-shell, console): one derived declaration for FormSectionSpec/FormViewSpec (#5653)
86d89d016  refactor(console): delete the deprecated zero-caller useBranding hook (#5651)
78cbdb530  refactor(types)!: retire ThemeComponentSchema … (#5489) (#5650)
8ebd57fc5  docs(core): qualify both `evaluateExpression` references in the JSDoc (#5649)
2d36552d2  Pin @objectstack/* to 17.1.0 (#5529)          ← the only dependency movement
```

And `2d36552d2`'s lockfile diff does not merely bump a version — **it introduces the package**:

```
- '@objectstack/spec@17.0.0':        →  + '@objectstack/spec@17.1.0':
- '@objectstack/formula@17.0.0':     →  + '@objectstack/formula@17.1.0':
+ pg-connection-string@2.14.0:
+     pg-connection-string: 2.14.0
```

`pg-connection-string` **was not in the dependency graph before this commit.** It arrives with the 17.0.0 → 17.1.0 bump, and 17.1.0 is exactly the version in the failing import trace.

The only other commit touching a boundary-relevant path is `8ebd57fc5`, and it is a **JSDoc-only** edit to `packages/core/src/evaluator/`. It changes shipped bytes (this package's `tsc` preserves comments) but cannot create an import.

## What this settles, and what it changes

**Candidate 1 in the card — "a dependency movement, the #5529 pin surface" — is confirmed. Candidate 2, a bundler-boundary regression, is excluded.** Nothing in the window newly pulls `packages/core`'s evaluator into `packages/components`' entry.

That makes triage's ⛔ *more* binding rather than less. The instruction was:

> Don't paper over it with a Turbopack `fs` shim/alias without knowing which — a shim over a real boundary regression ships `pg-connection-string` to browsers as accepted cargo.

We now know which, and the answer does not license the shim — it relocates the defect. The live question is no longer "what did objectui break" but:

> **Why does `@objectstack/spec@17.1.0` — a schema package that browser code imports — depend on a Postgres connection-string parser at all, and why does that dependency reach its browser-facing entry (`dist/index.mjs`) unconditionally?**

That is a **framework-side** question. `pg-connection-string`'s own line 88 is guarded (`config.sslcert || config.sslkey || config.sslrootcert ? require('fs') : null`) — the module is written to be Node-only and is being asked to resolve in a client graph. A bundler alias would make the build pass while still shipping a Postgres connection parser into the browser bundle as accepted cargo, which is precisely what the ⛔ forbids.

## Dispatching now, scoped accordingly

The dispatch is **verify-then-route**, not fix-blind: confirm the above independently, then establish whether `@objectstack/spec` 17.1.0 exposes that dependency through a browser condition or unconditionally. If the correct repair is upstream, this becomes a seam handoff to `objectstack` (the objectstack#10812 convention, as used for objectstack#11029) rather than something to force locally.

Interim options exist — reverting the pin, or a scoped bundler exclusion — but neither is this seat's to pick unilaterally, because #5529 pinned to 17.1.0 for its own stated reasons and reverting trades one breakage for whatever that pin was fixing. Those go up as a recommendation with evidence.

Out of scope, stated so it is not chased: `main` is also red on `Test (coverage)` (#5402, failing 100% since 2026-08-16) and that is a separate known-broken gauge. The queue-never-runs half stays on #4986, per triage.

## What was measured, in short

**The PM's hypothesis was right, and it is now a single-commit measurement rather than an inference.**

| objectui commit | `@objectstack/spec` | site build |
|---|---|---|
| `aa3b81062` (= `2d36552d2^`) | 17.0.0 | **GREEN** — `Tasks: 29 successful, 29 total`, turbo exit `0` |
| `2d36552d2` (#5529) | 17.1.0 | **RED** — `Can't resolve 'fs'`, `28 successful, 29 total`, turbo exit `1` |
| `6ff0eb1e7` (`origin/main`) | 17.1.0 | **RED** — identical trace and tally |

**The live question is answered, and the answer routes the card out of this repo.**

`@objectstack/spec@17.1.0` declares `pg-connection-string` in hard `dependencies`, imports it on **line 2 of `dist/index.mjs`** — top-level, static, unconditional — and its `exports` map contains **zero** `browser` conditions (no `browser` field either), on the published tarball and on objectstack `origin/main` (`3e26359`) alike. Six of sixteen entry points carry the import: root, `./cloud`, `./data`, `./kernel`, `./shared`, `./system`. The single call site is `pgParseableUrl()`, a **publish-time** Zod `superRefine` refusing a postgres datasource `config.url`, from `packages/spec/src/data/driver/postgres.zod.ts:16`.

**The tempting one-line fix does not work, and that is measured.** `@objectstack/formula` imports `createEvalUser` from the spec **root barrel** (`src/stdlib.ts:17`), and `createEvalUser` lives in `./identity`, which is clean — so re-pointing that import looks sufficient. It is not: the same `dist/index.mjs` also imports `@objectstack/spec/data` (lines 1607–1608), and `./data` is poisoned.

**Why the shim stays forbidden, more strongly than triage put it.** An `fs` alias would make the build green *and work at runtime* — the `require('fs')` branch is only reached for `?sslcert=`/`?sslkey=`/`?sslrootcert=`, which this same schema refuses one step earlier. That is what makes it dangerous: it would succeed, so nothing would ever prompt anyone to look again.

**Routed upstream:** **objectstack-ai/objectstack#11072** (`pm:queue` + `pm:blocking` + `domain:spec`), following the objectstack#10812 convention.

`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#11072`

That line is placed here rather than edited into this card's body: the body belongs to the filing seat, and per shared-identity discipline this seat does not rewrite another actor's post. Triage or the PM may want to lift it into the body, where the unlock scan reads it.

**No PR, deliberately.** The branch `claude/issue-5668-spec-1710-pg-connection-string` was pushed as the claim's landing marker and a write-routing probe; it carries no commits, because no objectui change is both correct and in scope. Every candidate is either the forbidden shim, a revert that trades this red for a `Type Check` red and undoes the #5531 ruling, or an architecture change to the docs site to route around a producer's defect.

**One process note, measured.** The bare footer form is **stripped by GitHub's sanitizer on issue creation** — #11072's body came back with the trailing `---` and footer gone entirely, byte-identical otherwise. Re-adding it in the session-URL form survived the edit intact. Worth knowing for anyone filing cards from a dispatch that prescribes the bare form.

## Measured to one commit, cause is upstream. Routed to objectstack#11072. Two decisions now sit with the maintainer.

The dispatch confirmed the PM's lockfile hypothesis **independently and by build**, then narrowed it past what the lockfile alone could show.

### The one-legged bisect

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| `aa3b81062` (= `2d36552d2^`) | **GREEN** — `Tasks: 29 successful, 29 total`, `TURBO_EXIT=0` |
| `2d36552d2` — *Pin @objectstack/\* to 17.1.0 (#5529)* | **RED** — `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'`, `Tasks: 28 successful, 29 total`, `TURBO_EXIT=1` |
| `6ff0eb1e7` (`origin/main` today) | **RED**, identically — same trace, same two MDX routes |

⚠️ **`--frozen-lockfile` was load-bearing on the green leg, and this is worth recording:** every objectui manifest declares `^17.0.0`, so a non-frozen install re-resolves to **17.1.0** and would have reddened the green leg **for the wrong reason** — producing a "both legs red, therefore not the cause" conclusion that is exactly backwards. The symlinks were verified per leg (`packages/core`, `components`, `types`, `app-shell` → `@objectstack+spec@17.0.0` on green, `17.1.0` on red).

⚠️ Second instrument catch: the verify-lock wrapper's own `VERDICT` line reads `command-exit 0` because it wraps the **driver script**, not turbo. It is **not** the verdict for the build. Turbo's exit was captured separately, redirected to file before any pipe.

### The cause, and why it is not objectui's

`@objectstack/spec@17.1.0` declares `pg-connection-string` as a **hard runtime dependency** and imports it at the **top level of `dist/index.mjs` (line 2 — static, unconditional)**. It declares **zero `browser` export conditions and no `browser` field**, so a browser consumer and a Node consumer resolve *the same file by construction*.

**Six of its sixteen entry points carry the import** — root, `./cloud`, `./data`, `./kernel`, `./shared`, `./system`. The single call site is `pgParseableUrl()`, a **publish-time Zod `superRefine`** on a postgres datasource `config.url` (`packages/spec/src/data/driver/postgres.zod.ts:16`). Still unfixed on objectstack `origin/main` (`3e26359`).

**"Import a narrower subpath" is not an available mitigation, and that was measured rather than assumed.** objectui's exposure is **50 source files** — 27 via `/data`, 9 via `/shared`, 7 via `/kernel`, 5 via the root barrel, 1 each via `/system` and `/cloud`. objectui is *already* disciplined about subpaths (186 subpath imports vs 6 root-barrel in non-test source) and it did not help, because `./data` — the second-most-used entry in the repo — is poisoned too.

**Filed upstream: objectstack#11072** (`pm:queue` + `pm:blocking` + `domain:spec`), carrying the bisect table, the mechanism, four graded options and a ready-to-run reproduction.

### No objectui code was produced, deliberately

The shim is forbidden by triage, and the measurement makes that prohibition **stronger**: an `fs` alias would make the build green **and work at runtime** — the `require('fs')` branch is only taken for `?sslcert=` / `?sslkey=` / `?sslrootcert=`, which this same schema refuses one step earlier. So nothing would ever prompt anyone to look again, and a Postgres connection-string parser becomes **permanent accepted cargo in every ObjectUI browser bundle**.

**No ablation was run and none is claimed.** The one mutation worth trying (re-point `@objectstack/formula`'s root-barrel import at `@objectstack/spec/identity`) was abandoned on measurement — formula also imports `@objectstack/spec/data` at `dist/index.mjs:1607-1608`, and `./data` is equally poisoned. ⚠️ Independently: the candidate files are **hardlinked into the container-shared pnpm content-addressed store (link count 3)**, so editing them in place would have corrupted **every other agent's worktree**. Worth knowing before anyone tries an in-place `node_modules` experiment here.

## Decision 1 — what objectui does in the interim (maintainer's call)
